- If sentiment is consistently neutral or negative in recent history, model tends to overestimate prices; adjust forecast downward by 2–5% for 30-day horizon.
- After a sharp price spike (e.g., >10% from prior peak), model often overshoots and fails to correct; reduce forecast by 5–10% in next 5–7 days.
- When sentiment shows early positive signals (e.g., >0.20), model often underreacts; increase forecast by 3–7% to align with sentiment momentum.
- If model shows steady upward trend with no recent volatility, true outcome often reverses or dips; apply mean reversion by reducing forecast by 3–8% in next 10–15 days.
- For 30-day forecasts, if history shows strong downward trend (e.g., 3+ consecutive drops), model often fails to recognize continuation; add 1–3% downward bias to forecast.
- If sentiment history includes multiple small positive signals (e.g., 0.20–0.33), model may overfit to recent highs; cap forecast at 1–2% above recent peak unless sentiment confirms strong momentum.
